newsitem.title: FRANCE: PSA Peugeot Citroen's Calvet to run for parliament.
newsitem.headline: PSA Peugeot Citroen's Calvet to run for parliament.

text.p: Jacques Calvet, chairman of PSA Peugeot Citroen, said in an interview made public on Friday that he intended to be a candidate in France's May 25-June 1 parliamentary election.

Calvet, who served as a senior aide to former French president Valery Giscard d'Estaing, told the French daily Le Figaro that he would stand in a suburban Paris district as a candidate for the current centre-right majority rather than for any single party.
"I will stand on the presidential majority ticket," he said, expressing general support for the policies of conservative President Jacques Chirac.

"I have always had the idea of entering politics once my task had been accomplished at Peugeot-Citroen," he said. "I hope to be able to bring to the job some practical things that I have learned over the past 40 years and which could benefit the country."
However, Calvet made no mention of any plans to leave his post at the car maker.
